classification.difficultyReason: Follow explicit compass settings and labelling instructions, then check equal intervals using measurement or differences between successive radii.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Set your compasses to a radius of 8 cm. Then choose a point $O$ in the middle of your page and draw a circle with centre $O$ and radius 8 cm.

answer.short: Circle with centre $O$ and radius 8 cm.
answer.worked: Open the compasses to 8 cm using a ruler. Keep the compass point fixed at $O$ and turn the pencil through a complete circle without changing the opening.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Change the setting of the compasses to 6 cm and draw a circle with the same centre $O$ and radius 6 cm.

answer.short: Second circle with centre $O$ and radius 6 cm.
answer.worked: Set the compass opening to 6 cm. Keeping the point at the same centre $O$, draw a complete circle inside the first circle.

inlines.text: Repeat this process, drawing circles with centre
because they all have the same centre.

answer.short: Four concentric circles with radii 8 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm and 2 cm.
answer.worked: Keep the compass point at $O$. Draw one circle with an opening of 4 cm and another with an opening of 2 cm. All four circles have centre $O$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Draw a horizontal line through the centre $O$. From left to right, label the eight points where the line intersects the circles with the letters $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$, $F$, $G$ and $H$.

answer.short: The points lie in the order $A,B,C,D,O,E,F,G,H$ from left to right.
answer.worked: Draw a horizontal line through $O$ across all four circles. Label the intersections from left to right: $A$ on the 8 cm circle, $B$ on the 6 cm circle, $C$ on the 4 cm circle and $D$ on the 2 cm circle; then $E$, $F$, $G$ and $H$ on the corresponding circles to the right of $O$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Check that the eight intervals $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DO$, $OE$, $EF$, $FG$ and $GH$ all have the same lengths.

answer.short: All eight intervals have length 2 cm.
answer.worked: On either side of $O$, successive radii differ by $8-6=2$ cm, $6-4=2$ cm and $4-2=2$ cm. The innermost radius is 2 cm, so $DO=OE=2$ cm also. Therefore $AB=BC=CD=DO=OE=EF=FG=GH=2\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Completed shared construction: four concentric circles and their labelled intersections with one horizontal line. Ordinary geometry and point markers use black.
spec.mathematics: Centre O; radii 8, 6, 4 and 2 cm. Horizontal coordinates relative to O are A=-8, B=-6, C=-4, D=-2, E=2, F=4, G=6 and H=8 cm. Every consecutive interval, including those adjacent to O, is 2 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the student constructs the complete figure.
